metaDescription: Six Lefant robot vacuums from the slim M210 to the 20,000 Pa M210 Omni, compared by navigation, dock type, mop design and ownership costs.
expertTake: The Lefant M210 Omni is the top pick because it combines a roller mop, a self-washing base and a body only 3.35 in tall. The M210 is the value pick for hard floors, with a slim body and a physical routine. Buyers who need strict obstacle recognition should skip this brand and look at camera models.
introParagraphs: This is a budget-leaning brand that has quietly built a full ladder, from plain thin robots to laser-mapped docks with roller mops. The price tiers are low for what the spec sheets promise, which makes the details of each model worth checking.

The sensible approach is to match the model to the home, not the peak number. Navigation type, dock style and mop design change the daily routine far more than the suction figure, and these are the areas where the lineup differs the most.

products.name: Lefant M210 Omni, 20,000 Pa, roller mop, self-wash and dry base
products.description:
The M210 Omni uses a roller mop with a real-time fresh-water system, so the surface touching your floor is rinsed while the robot runs. The body is only 85 mm, about 3.35 in, tall and 280 mm wide, which lets it go under sofas that stop most mop stations. A self-cleaning and self-drying base handles the roller afterwards.

Top of the price ladder here, it carries the highest suction label, 20,000 Pa. That is a peak figure, and the roller and brush do more for hard-floor results than the motor does. Compared with the M3 it swaps flat pads for the roller and drops the hot-water wash.

Upkeep centres on the base: wipe the tray, empty the dirty tank, and check the drain for lint after each week of use. The tangle-free roller needs the usual monthly trim, and roller replacements are the main consumable. Over a year of weekly mopping, plan on at least one spare roller and a few filters, and keep the base away from carpet so the drain tray never leaks onto a rug.
products.bestFor: Hard-floor homes with low furniture that want a roller mop.
pros: Roller mop is sprayed with fresh water in real time
3.35 in body fits under low sofas
Base cleans and dries the roller
Highest suction label of the six
cons: Top price tier of the brand

products.name: Lefant M3, 12,000 Pa, 3.2 L bag, 45 C hot-water mop dock
products.description:
The M3 is built around its dock. A 3.2 L bag lets the base go up to 90 days between changes, the mop pads are washed with 45 C water to dissolve grease and cool air then dries them. The robot itself offers 12,000 Pa and obstacle avoidance on the way.

The M3 gives up the roller of the M210 Omni for flat pads, so dried spills are less thoroughly lifted, and the 45 C wash is cooler than the 212 F boil washes of some premium brands. In return it sits a tier lower. For a household that wants hands-off pads and bags, it is the better balanced pick.

The extra tanks are the cost. Empty the dirty-water tank after each run, wipe the wash tray and replace the pads when they stop absorbing. The 90 day figure is a best case, so check the bag early in a home with pets. Because the base also washes pads, it is worth placing it on hard flooring with a bit of room to open the lid and lift out the tanks without moving the whole unit.
products.bestFor: Busy households that want a long bag interval and washed pads.
pros: 3.2 L bag rated for up to 90 days
Pads washed with 45 C water
Cool-air drying prevents mildew
Mid price tier among the docks
cons: Dirty tank needs emptying each run

products.name: Lefant M2 Plus, 6,000 Pa, LiDAR, 75-day dock, multi-floor maps
products.description:
The M2 Plus is the sensible laser-guided pick. A LiDAR scanner builds the map, multi-floor memory stores several levels, and no-go zones keep it from pet bowls. The dock comes with two 2.5 L bags and the maker quotes up to 75 days between changes, and the robot runs about 140 minutes.

Its 6,000 Pa is modest next to the M3 at 12,000 Pa, and a pad mop is present but plain. The attraction is navigation and the dock at a lower tier than the M3. For a two-storey flat with mostly hard floors, it covers the essentials.

Bag swaps are the main upkeep. Wipe the laser window, clean the cliff sensors and check the dock filter. The two bags in the box mean you do not buy refills for roughly half a year. Its multi-floor memory is the feature worth testing first, because a map that survives being carried upstairs saves the setup work for each level.
products.bestFor: Two-storey homes that want mapping and a dock on a budget.
pros: LiDAR with multi-floor map storage
Two bags included for the dock
140 minute runtime covers large floors
No-go zones for pet bowls and cables

products.name: Lefant M330 Pro, dToF LiDAR, 190 degree PSD obstacle avoidance
products.description:
The M330 Pro uses a dToF laser that scans up to 15 m and a 190 degree PSD sensor that measures distance to objects ahead. That combination is aimed at avoiding furniture legs and cords without a camera. Carpet detection keeps it from wetting rugs in mop mode.

It has a 450 ml visible dustbin and no self-empty dock, which keeps the price low, and it costs less than the M2 Plus. The PSD sensor does not identify an object, so socks and cables remain a risk. Think of it as a better navigator than the M210 line and a cheaper one than the dock models.

You empty the bin by hand and see the contents through the window. Rinse the mop pad, wipe the PSD window and clear hair from the tangle-free brush. With no dock, the only recurring parts are pads and filters. Its dToF scanner makes the first mapping run quick, so run it with doors open and chairs pushed in to get a clean outline of the rooms.
products.bestFor: Mid-size homes that want laser mapping without a dock.
pros: dToF scan reaches up to 15 m
190 degree PSD sensor eases furniture navigation
Carpet detection skips rugs in mop mode
Visible bin shows when it needs emptying
cons: Sensor does not identify cables or socks
450 ml bin fills quickly with pets

products.name: Lefant M210P, 4,000 Pa, 200 minute runtime, 2.99 in slim
products.description:
The M210P is the endurance model. A 200 minute battery is a long run for a plain robot, and a 2.99 in body slips under furniture. It evolved from the M210 with stronger suction, 4,000 Pa, quieter running and a tangle-free brush for pet hair.

It has no map, no dock and no mop, so it behaves like a classic bump-and-turn robot with a big battery. Against the M2 Plus it gives up mapping and the dock, and in return it costs much less. A small apartment gets all the benefit of the long runtime and none of the dock upkeep.

Empty the bin after each run, rinse the filter, snip hair from the brush and replace the side brush when its bristles splay. There are no bags to buy and no water parts to descale. Because it has no map, it will cross the same strip twice now and then, which is the cost of the long battery and the bargain price.
products.bestFor: Small apartments that want simple, long daily runs.
pros: 200 minute runtime for a plain robot
2.99 in body fits under low beds
Tangle-free brush for pet hair
No bag or water costs

products.name: Lefant M210, 120 minute runtime, slim body, app and Alexa
products.description:
The M210 is the plainest model in the family and the original of the line. It is an 11 in disc with a 120 minute battery, automatic return to charge and control through an app or a voice assistant. It is aimed at pet households with hard floors and light carpet.

It has no mapping, so it covers floors by pattern, and no dock, so you empty it by hand. Against the M210P it gives up 80 minutes of battery and some suction, and it costs the least in the lineup. It is also the easiest to hand to a relative who does not want settings, since the main button starts a run and the rest can be ignored. For a bedroom or small flat it is enough.

Upkeep is the usual few minutes: empty the bin, wash the filter, trim the brush and refresh the side brush. It connects through the dedicated Lefant app, so read the pairing steps in the manual before setup.
products.bestFor: Small flats on a tight budget with hard floors.
pros: Lowest price tier of the six
App and voice assistant control
Automatic return to the charger
Slim disc fits under most furniture
cons: No mapping, so coverage is patterned

buyingCriteria.explanation: The M2 Plus and M330 Pro use laser scanning, and the M210 and M210P use sensors only. Laser machines plan rows and remember rooms, which matters above about 600 sq ft. Below that, a plain robot with a long battery is enough.
The M210 Omni has a roller with live water spray, and the M3 washes flat pads at 45 C. A roller lifts dried spills and a pad smears them. Choose the roller if you mop weekly.
The M3 uses a 3.2 L bag for up to 90 days, and the M2 Plus ships with two 2.5 L bags for 75 days. A dock is a chore saver, not a necessity. The M210 family has none, so you empty the bin yourself.

The M210 Omni stands 3.35 in tall, and the M210P stands 2.99 in. Measure under your sofa and bed. A robot that cannot enter the room is wasted. Remember that a mop base needs floor space too, usually about the width of a chair, so check the wall spot as well.
The M330 Pro uses a 190 degree PSD sensor, which detects distance and not identity. Cables and socks can still tangle it. For cluttered floors you must tidy first or use no-go zones.

The M210P offers 200 minutes and the M2 Plus 140 minutes. A longer battery means fewer recharge breaks on a big floor. Check the real area against the rated runtime. Boost mode on carpet drains the pack quickly, so a house with rugs should assume the runtime is nearer half the headline figure.

specDecoder.meaning: A direct time-of-flight laser measures distance by timing the light pulse. It builds a map and works in the dark.
specDecoder.watchFor: The M330 Pro quotes a 15 m scan, which exceeds the size of most rooms.

specDecoder.meaning: A position-sensitive device measures how far an object is by the angle of reflected light. It judges distance, not shape or identity.
specDecoder.watchFor: The M330 Pro uses a 190 degree PSD window, and the M2L Plus pairs nine sensors with a 190 degree field.

specDecoder.meaning: The peak motor pull at the maker's strongest mode. Brand to brand it is not directly comparable.
specDecoder.watchFor: The M210 Omni lists 20,000 Pa and the M210P lists 4,000 Pa, yet both clean hard floors.

specDecoder.meaning: Water temperature in the dock's pad wash. Hotter water cuts grease better.
specDecoder.watchFor: The M3 washes at 45 C, which is warm rather than hot.

specDecoder.meaning: Minutes of running at standard power before returning to charge. Boost modes cut it sharply.
specDecoder.watchFor: The M210P quotes 200 minutes, and the M210 quotes 120 minutes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Navigation
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared laser, PSD and sensor-only designs. The M330 Pro and M2 Plus lead, while the M210 line follows pattern coverage. Map storage helped two-storey homes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mop design
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked the M210 Omni roller above the flat pads of the M3 for dried spills. The M3 earned credit for 45 C washing. Models with no mop were judged on dry cleaning.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dock
howWeEvaluated.description: We read bag size, bag count and pad wash. The M3 at 3.2 L and the M2 Plus with two 2.5 L bags set the standard. Missing docks were judged on bin size.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit and battery
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared heights, like 3.35 in on the Omni and 2.99 in on the M210P, and runtimes from 120 to 200 minutes. Clearance decides where a robot can go. Battery drives how large a floor it can clean.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed recurring owner reports about app pairing, dock jams and brush wear. Patterns outweighed single remarks. The separate Lefant app is a known setup snag.

cards.label: Roller
cards.text: The M210 Omni sprays fresh water on a spinning roller and washes it in the base. It scrubs dried spots and costs more.

cards.label: Flat pads
cards.text: The M3 spins or wipes pads that are washed with 45 C water. Pads are cheaper but smear stubborn stains.

howToChoose.note: Choose the roller for weekly mopping and the pads for occasional damp passes.

rows: Dock with two bags in the box

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A body under about 3.5 in and no tall laser dome. Measure the gap and allow a margin.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The M210P at 2.99 in is the lowest, and the M210 Omni at 3.35 in is the best low roller option. Laser models sit taller.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You mop weekly or have two floors. The M210 Omni and M2 Plus remove the manual work.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small, mostly hard-floor home. The M210 or M210P covers it.

maintenance.interval: After each run on no-dock models
maintenance.why: A full bin chokes airflow. The M330 Pro has a visible 450 ml bin so you can see when.
Dirty mop surfaces spread grime and smell. Dry them in open air.
The M3 and M2 Plus bags are quoted at 90 and 75 days. Change them earlier in pet homes.
Dust blurs the sensors and causes strange paths. Use a dry cloth.
Wrapped hair slows the roller and strains the motor. Cut it along the groove.

faq.a: The brand uses its own app, and setup trouble is a common owner complaint. Follow the manual's connection steps and use a 2.4 GHz network where required. The M210 family can also run without it.

faq.q: Which Lefant is best for pet hair?
faq.a: The M210P and M210 Omni both list tangle-free roller designs. The M210 Omni adds a roller mop. Trim any brush every couple of weeks.
The PSD and laser sensors avoid furniture, but they do not identify cables or socks. Tidy them first or set no-go zones. Camera models do this better.
No. The number is a peak figure and the roller and brush matter more. The real strength of the M210 Omni is the roller mop and low height.

faq.q: How long do the dock bags last?
faq.a: The M3 quotes up to 90 days and the M2 Plus 75 days. Pet hair shortens both. Check at one month.

faq.q: Does the M210 work without Wi-Fi?
faq.a: The M210 is sold with Wi-Fi, app and voice assistant control, so it expects a connection for scheduling. Cleaning can still be started from the robot itself. Check the manual for the exact controls on your unit.
